dialog.body: City of Newport, Public Works, this is Denise. How can I help you?
Hi, Denise. My name is Eleanor Pucci. I'm at 701 Thames Street, on the corner at Wellington. I'm calling about the storm drain on my corner. Again.
Okay, Mrs. Pucci. 701 Thames. What's going on with the drain?

It backed up in last week's nor'easter. The whole corner was a pond Sunday night, and the water came right in through the basement windows and the floor drain. I've got about four inches down there. I took the morning off work to deal with it.
I'm sorry. That's awful. Is anyone hurt, any electrical down there, anything like that?

Nobody's hurt. I shut the breaker for the basement. The furnace is up on blocks, thank God, my late husband did that years ago. But that's not the point. This is the second time this winter. It did the exact same thing in January after that coastal storm. We called then too, my son called. Somebody came out, looked at the grate, and left.
Okay. Let me pull up the address. [pause] I do see a call from January for 701 Thames, drain backup, and it looks like a crew cleared debris off the grate on the twelfth.

They pulled some leaves off the top. That's not the problem. The problem is under the street. Every time it rains hard, it comes back up out of that drain instead of going down it. It's not leaves, Denise. I'm not an engineer, but I know what I'm looking at.
I hear you. I'm going to put this in as a repeat backup, not just a grate cleaning, so the crew knows it's happened twice and that the basement took water both times.
Please. Because I've been patient. I've been very patient. I'm done being patient. I'm not yelling at you, it's not your fault, but somebody has to actually look at that pipe.
Understood. When would you be home for a crew? They'll want to look at the corner and probably the basement drain too.
I can't take another morning. Thursday I'm home after noon. Before that, no.
Okay. I can get a Public Works crew to the corner on Thursday. I'll note afternoon, after twelve, and that they should knock on the door at 701 so you can show them the basement.
Thursday. Fine. And I want somebody above the crew to call me. Not a work order number. A person who can tell me what the city is going to do about that drain, because I can't do this a third time.
That's fair. I'll ask my supervisor to call you back. What's the best number?
My cell, four oh one, five five five, oh one four two.
Four oh one, five five five, oh one four two. Got it. I'll flag it for a supervisor callback, and I'll put in the note that this is the second flood this winter at the same address.

Thank you. Now, while I have you. I got a notice that I'm behind on the water and sewer. It says ninety dollars overdue, and it said something about a lien. I don't want that hanging over the house on top of everything else. Can I just pay it now?

Yes, I can take that for you. Utilities billing is in the same system. Let me bring up the account. [pause] Yes, I see it. Ninety dollars past due on the water and sewer account for 701 Thames. Do you want to pay the full ninety today?
The full ninety. Get it off the books.
Okay. Credit or debit?
Credit. You ready? Four one one one, one one one one, one one one one, one one one one.
And the expiration?
Oh nine, twenty-eight. And the code on the back is one two three.
Name on the card, Eleanor Pucci?
Eleanor M. Pucci.

Okay, give me one second. [pause] That went through. Ninety dollars applied to the water and sewer account. Your balance is zero, and that takes care of the overdue notice. You'll get a receipt in the mail, or I can email it.
Mail is fine. So that's done. No lien.
No lien. It's paid in full as of this morning.
Good. One less thing.

So, just to read it back. A Public Works crew comes to Thames and Wellington on Thursday, afternoon, and knocks at 701 to see the basement. It's logged as a repeat drain backup, second basement flood this winter. My supervisor calls you back on your cell. And the ninety dollars is paid.
That's it. Thursday, and a call from a supervisor. I'm going to hold you to both.
You should. And if water comes back up before Thursday, call the Public Works line right away, even after hours, and tell them you have an open repeat backup.
If it rains again before Thursday, I'll be calling a lot more than the Public Works line. Okay. Thank you, Denise. You've been decent about it.
Of course. I'm sorry you're dealing with this again, Mrs. Pucci. Take care.
Yeah. Bye.
